Definition: from G3408; to let out for wages, i.e. (middle voice) to hire:--hire.
BiblicalUsage: The word is to hire, to take on labourers for wages, and it appears twice in the parable of the vineyard: the householder went out early in the morning to hire labourers, and the men standing idle in the marketplace answer, because no man hath hired us.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the hiring is the grace of the parable: the householder goes out again and again, and no one who wants work is left standing idle.
RelatedEvents: The Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard
